newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil tax-free sugar exports still under study.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax-free sugar exports still under study.

text.p: Tax exemption for an extra 500,000 tonnes of Brazilian sugar exports is still being studied by the Finance Ministry, more than a month after the Ministry of Industry and Commerce authorized the sales, an official said.
Pedro Cabral, head of the sugar and alcohol department in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said market conditions had changed since the original export authorization was issued in December.
"The tax exemption (for the extra sugar exports) is still being studied by the Finance Ministry," Cabral told Reuters.
"The market has changed (since the extra export quota was authorized). External prices are down, internal prices are up."
Cabral said he did not know when Finance Minister Pedro Malan would sign a decree exempting the exports from tax.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce passed the decree to the Finance Ministry early in January but it has languished in Malan's office since with little explanation for the delay.
An aide to the minister said he was unaware of the fate of the decree.

The extra 500,000 tonnes were themselves authorized in a decree published in the government's Official Journal in December. They are in addition to the 5.2 million tonnes of exports orginally set in the 1996/97 sugar crop plan.

Traders note that the additional export quota will have little immediate effect because most mills have no produce left to ship. They say they are likely to either sell their quotas to other mills or use them for the next crop.
Cabral declined to comment on how much sugar was available for export. "I don't know about that," he said.
